correctness.rationale: For prescribed indegrees, the fixed-event probability at r distinct vertices is the product of their target multiplicities divided by (n)_r. This proves PGF=sum e_r(d)(z-1)^r/(n)_r. A unit transfer (A,B)->(A-1,B+1), A>=B+2, changes the symmetric-polynomial product by delta t^2 times the other-factor product. Because remaining multiplicities sum <=n-2, the quotient is the genuine PGF of an injection-success statistic H. The exact PGF increment is delta (z-1)^2 E[z^H]/(n(n-1)), hence exactly the positive discrete second difference for all convex test functions and strictness for strictly convex tests. Integral majorization is generated by these transfers. The mean and variance follow from the first two factorial moments. Independent rational enumerator executed with 4,372 exact assertions for n=2..8.

source_inspections.title: A limit theorem for the six-length of random functional graphs with a fixed degree sequence

value.rationale: Conditional indegrees are a natural structural constraint on random functional digraphs, and loop count is a natural local cycle statistic. The result orders the ENTIRE distribution for every convex loss as target indegrees are balanced, supplies an exact signed-probability second-difference measure for each move, and identifies unique extremal profiles up to permutation. This is substantially stronger than the familiar mean-one fact or its Schur-concave variance formula; it is useful for degree-constrained loop-count uncertainty and comparisons with the random permutation endpoint.
